_README: L1 classifications for batch seed=42, n=120. PROVENANCE MATTERS HERE, so read this. These were produced by Claude (Sonnet-class), one pass, temperature not controlled, via a subagent harness rather than by app.classifier.LLMClassifier calling the Anthropic API. The model saw ONLY the fields a real L1 receives - the Razorpay error object, instrument, issuer, amount, kind and customer history - and was given app.classifier.SYSTEM_PROMPT verbatim as its instructions. It never saw ground_truth, the bucket label, the ambiguity flags, or sim/generate_batch.py. WHY THAT MATTERS: whoever writes the batch generator knows the answer key, so a classification produced by that same context would be contaminated and the accuracy figures would be meaningless. Four separate fresh contexts did the work, 30 cases each. WHAT THIS IS NOT: a live API run. app.classifier.LLMClassifier is the production path and remains untested against the real endpoint. Replaying this file is deterministic; re-running the model is not, and would not reproduce these exact labels.

case_0034.rationale: source=bank at step=payment_authorization with reason=null and only the generic description 'Payment failed' — the issuer gave no cause, so no specific failure mode can be asserted. AXIS card, amount_inr 3915.43 sits below the customer's typical 5540.59, which argues against a limit trip and weakens a funds read. tenure_days 133 with successful_payments 6 and prior_failures_90d 2 is a middling, not clean, record; prior_contacts_30d 1 five days ago leaves room for one more touch. A short deferral avoids stacking a second authorization attempt into the same issuer window.

case_0010.rationale: reason=card_blocked from source=bank at payment_authorization is an issuer state on the PNB card, not a condition that changes with time, so re-presenting the same token is wasted. The customer side is strong: tenure_days 479, successful_payments 8, prior_failures_90d 0, and amount_inr 697.29 is close to their typical 531.39 — nothing here suggests unwillingness to pay, only a dead card. prior_contacts_30d 1 at 10 days ago means an instrument-update ask is not fatiguing. Note the block itself may be risk-driven at the issuer, but nothing in the payload says so.

That rules out a retry on principle regardless of the missing reason. case_0009.rationale: reason=insufficient_funds with source=customer at payment_authorization on the IDFC_FIRST card is a balance shortfall, structurally recoverable. case_0065.rationale: reason=payment_otp_timeout with source=customer at step=payment_authentication means the IDFC_FIRST card was never authorised, so a re-presentment has nothing to present — only a fresh link recovers this. case_0059.rationale: reason=payment_limit_exceeded from source=bank at payment_authorization on an AXIS card, with amount_inr 2695.60 sitting under the customer's typical 3664.18 — the same signature as the other limit cases here, and the strongest available reading is a daily cap already spent elsewhere today rather than a ceiling this invoice exceeds on its own. case_0046.rationale: reason=payment_cancelled_by_customer at step=payment_authentication with source=customer means the YES_BANK card was never authorised; a retry is structurally incapable of fixing this and only a fresh link can. Unlike the other cancellation in this batch, the record here is strong — tenure_days 484, successful_payments 18, prior_failures_90d 1 — and amount_inr 4896.07 is close to their typical 5339.20, so the likeliest story is an interrupted 3DS session rather than a decision not to buy. prior_contacts_30d 0 with days_since_last_contact null means the channel is completely fresh, so the link can go out immediately.

case_0061.rationale: The free-text description says 'Payment declined by the issuing bank' but reason=issuer_not_available. I trust the structured reason: the description field is Razorpay's generic customer-facing string for the whole bank-decline family, while reason is the mapped code, and an unreachable PNB switch is an outage that clears rather than a decision that stands. The bucket is capped at MEDIUM by the customer, not the code — tenure_days 42 with successful_payments 1 and prior_failures_90d 1 — though amount_inr 1690.76 well under typical 2438.76 helps. If a scheduled retry returns the same pair, the deliberate-decline reading should be revisited.

case_0012.rationale: The description 'Payment failed. Please retry after some time.' invites exactly the wrong action; reason=card_blocked from source=bank is the field I trust, because the description is a generic customer-facing string Razorpay attaches broadly while reason carries the issuer's mapped state. A YES_BANK card the issuer has blocked will decline identically forever, so following the description would burn attempts and possibly trip issuer velocity limits. The customer is worth the update ask: tenure_days 541, successful_payments 16, prior_failures_90d 0, prior_contacts_30d 0, and amount_inr 655.14 is below their typical 1010.49, so the sum is trivial next to the relationship.

case_0068.rationale: reason=account_closed on the ICICI card is as terminal as this taxonomy gets — the underlying account no longer exists — so the description's 'Please retry after some time' is misleading boilerplate and the structured reason wins. Because kind=RECURRING, the standing mandate died with the account and the customer must re-authorise on a new instrument rather than merely restate a card number. Recovery odds are nonetheless good: tenure_days 706, successful_payments 19, prior_failures_90d 0, prior_contacts_30d 0, and amount_inr 10760.73 is in line with their typical 10007.17, so this reads as a banking change rather than a departure.

case_0048.rationale: reason=issuer_not_available with the description 'Issuer or switch is inoperative' is an infrastructure outage at YES_BANK, the clearest transient signature available, and description and reason agree rather than conflict. Unlike the other netbanking case here, kind=RECURRING means an e-mandate exists and can be re-presented without the customer, so an automated retry is genuinely available. Everything else supports the top bucket: tenure_days 755, successful_payments 18, prior_failures_90d 0, prior_contacts_30d 0, and amount_inr 332.96 is small and below their typical 526.23. The four-day gap follows mastercard_advice_code 27.

case_0027.rationale: reason=account_closed on the HDFC card is terminal and overrides the description's 'Please retry after some time', so no retry path exists. The instrument fix and the relationship prognosis diverge sharply here: successful_payments 0 over tenure_days 43 with prior_failures_90d 3 and prior_contacts_30d 2 at days_since_last_contact 6.0 describes an account that has never once collected and has already absorbed two contacts. amount_inr 798.86 against typical 1031.38 makes the recoverable sum small relative to the effort. One final update request is defensible because a closed account can be a genuine bank switch; if it goes unanswered this should stop rather than cycle.

case_0052.rationale: reason=payment_declined_risk from source=bank at payment_authorization is HDFC asserting a fraud or compromise signal, and the bland description 'Your payment could not be processed' is deliberately uninformative to the payer, as such messages are. Retrying would re-present an instrument the issuer has already flagged, and messaging the customer would confirm to whoever currently holds that card which instrument is being tested — so both automated levers are off. The customer record — tenure_days 170, successful_payments 11, prior_failures_90d 2, amount_inr 2300.65 against typical 2632.82 — is unremarkable, which is itself worth a human's attention: it fits a compromised card on a legitimate account. Human review only.

The person is a 405-day ICICI card customer with 21 successful_payments, prior_failures_90d=0 and prior_contacts_30d=0, and this 13169.96 INR charge is well under their typical_invoice_paise of 2041462 (20414.62 INR), so this reads as an interrupted session rather than refusal to pay, and they have zero contact fatigue to work against.

case_0018.rationale: The description 'Payment failed. Please retry after some time.' is Razorpay's generic customer-facing template and invites exactly the wrong action; the structured reason=mandate_revoked is the specific machine-readable field and is corroborated by kind=RECURRING, so I trust reason over description. A revoked e-mandate on this ICICI card cannot be re-presented at any interval — the standing authorisation is gone and must be re-collected. Odds are poor: despite tenure_days=562 there are only 3 successful_payments against prior_failures_90d=7, and prior_contacts_30d=2 with days_since_last_contact=3.0 means this customer has already been asked twice this month about a 1526.04 INR charge that sits above their typical_invoice_paise of 122510 (1225.10 INR).

case_0095.rationale: reason=payment_failed with source=bank at step=payment_authorization is an SBI issuer decision with no stated cause, which Razorpay documents as normal for bank declines rather than a malformed payload, so I will not invent a precise cause. The history is middling and does not push the estimate either way hard: tenure_days=387 with 6 successful_payments and prior_failures_90d=2, and 12482.17 INR is close to typical_invoice_paise 1203637 (12036.37 INR), so amount shock is not the driver. prior_contacts_30d=0 leaves room to act, and a single spaced re-presentment is the cheapest way to distinguish a one-off issuer refusal from a standing one before spending a customer contact.

case_0040.rationale: An unexplained source=bank refusal at payment_authorization from ICICI against a customer with tenure_days=717, successful_payments=29 and prior_failures_90d=0 is far more likely to be a momentary issuer-side decision than a standing block — nothing in 717 days of history suggests this card is dead. The 13218.95 INR charge runs about 18 percent over typical_invoice_paise 1122549 (11225.49 INR), which is enough to trip a velocity or amount check without meaning anything permanent. prior_contacts_30d=0, so a silent re-presentment costs nothing in goodwill and should be tried before any message reaches a customer this clean.

Note the 6492.50 INR request is below this customer's typical_invoice_paise of 933175 (9331.75 INR), meaning the SBI daily cap was consumed by other spending rather than by this invoice being unusually large. I hold the estimate mid-range rather than high because prior_failures_90d=7 against only 8 successful_payments over tenure_days=409 suggests a recurring pattern, and prior_contacts_30d=3 with days_since_last_contact=2.0 means outreach is nearly exhausted if the retry fails.

case_0089.rationale: reason=card_lost_or_stolen from source=bank is an affirmative issuer statement about the instrument, and it is the one case where the customer history must not soften the handling: tenure_days=994, successful_payments=15 and prior_failures_90d=0 describe an excellent account, but if this SBI card is in someone else's hands then a dunning message about the 13661.42 INR charge tells that person which instrument to try next and which merchant is watching. No retry, no message — a human needs to verify identity out of band before anything is sent. Recovery on this invoice through the existing instrument is effectively nil regardless of the relationship's quality.

case_0088.rationale: reason=insufficient_funds with source=customer at payment_authorization is a balance condition on the SBI UPI account, not an instrument or authorisation problem, so the instrument stays valid and only timing needs fixing. The account is sound — tenure_days=309, successful_payments=8, prior_failures_90d=1 and prior_contacts_30d=0 — and the 3954.97 INR debit is about 21 percent over typical_invoice_paise 326567 (3265.67 INR), so a modest shortfall explains it. Today is the 1st, which is the worst point in the Indian pay cycle to re-present: salary credits cluster on the 28th-31st, so the deferral targets the 28th rather than burning an attempt into an empty account now.

case_0056.rationale: reason=issuer_not_available with source=bank is INDUSIND's switch being inoperative, which says nothing about this customer's willingness or ability to pay, and mastercard_advice_code=27 is the issuer's own instruction to re-present after roughly four days — I follow that rather than picking an interval myself. The mechanics favour recovery, but I hold the estimate mid-range because the relationship is thin: tenure_days=54 with only 1 successful_payment, and prior_contacts_30d=2 with days_since_last_contact=2.0 already on a 54-day-old account. The 2514.21 INR charge is below typical_invoice_paise 379833 (3798.33 INR), so amount is not a factor.

case_0004.rationale: reason=payment_failed_insufficient_funds with source=customer is a balance condition on the HDFC UPI account, and the pattern here is what lowers the estimate rather than the code: prior_failures_90d=6 against only 3 successful_payments over tenure_days=448 means failure is this account's normal state, not an exception. The 7052.29 INR request also runs about 30 percent above typical_invoice_paise 543221 (5432.21 INR), widening the gap that has to be closed. prior_contacts_30d=2 with days_since_last_contact=4.0 means messaging is already saturated, so the only lever left is timing — re-present after the 28th-31st salary window instead of today, the 1st.

case_0080.rationale: reason is null and the description is the bare 'Payment failed', so no cause is stated; what narrows it is source=customer at step=payment_authorization, which excludes gateway, network and issuer-unavailable causes and points at the payer's own PNB account rather than the rails. Against prior_failures_90d=6 with 7 successful_payments over tenure_days=546, a recurring 472.92 INR debit that is well under typical_invoice_paise 77808 (778.08 INR) failing at authorisation reads as an empty account. Confidence is low because a paused UPI mandate would present similarly. prior_contacts_30d=3 with days_since_last_contact=2.0 rules out more outreach, leaving a post-salary-window re-presentment as the only cheap move.

case_0055.rationale: reason is null and source=bank gives no cause, which Razorpay documents as ordinary for issuer declines, so the strongest signal in the payload is mastercard_advice_code=24 — INDUSIND telling us to re-present after about an hour, which is only issued for conditions the issuer expects to clear almost immediately. The customer supports acting straight away: tenure_days=512 with successful_payments=23, prior_failures_90d=1, prior_contacts_30d=0, and a 1773.77 INR charge comfortably below typical_invoice_paise 284395 (2843.95 INR). Nothing here needs the customer's attention, so the attempt should be spent before any message is.

case_0047.rationale: reason=payment_limit_exceeded is a per-transaction ceiling, not a daily one, so unlike a daily cap it does not reset overnight — re-presenting the same 2438.46 INR on the same INDUSIND card would fail identically, and the fix has to come from the customer raising the cap or paying on another instrument. The revealing detail is that 2438.46 INR sits below typical_invoice_paise 400811 (4008.11 INR), so the card itself carries an unusually low limit rather than this invoice being large. Odds are poor: tenure_days=7 with only 2 successful_payments, and days_since_last_contact=5.0 with prior_contacts_30d=1 on an account barely a week old, on a kind=RECURRING mandate that will keep hitting the same wall each cycle.

case_0008.rationale: reason=issuer_not_available with source=bank at payment_authorization is KOTAK's switch being down; it is infrastructure, not a decision about this payer, and such outages typically clear in minutes. The customer is the best in this batch — tenure_days=791, successful_payments=39, prior_failures_90d=0, prior_contacts_30d=0 — and the 4511.24 INR charge is under typical_invoice_paise 589000 (5890.00 INR), so there is no amount or behaviour signal arguing against an immediate re-presentment. With no mastercard_advice_code to specify an interval, and no customer action required, spending an attempt now is strictly cheaper than any message.

case_0090.rationale: source=customer at step=payment_authentication with reason=payment_cancelled_by_customer means the 3DS step was actively abandoned on this AXIS card, so nothing was authorised and re-presentment is impossible — only a fresh link would help. But the surrounding facts argue this was deliberate rather than accidental: the 2087.61 INR charge is roughly 58 percent above typical_invoice_paise 132394 (1323.94 INR), it is a kind=RECURRING debit, and the account is 18 days old with 2 successful_payments and prior_failures_90d=2. A customer who cancels at the OTP screen on a larger-than-usual recurring charge on a three-week-old subscription may be withdrawing from it; prior_contacts_30d=1 at days_since_last_contact=3.0 leaves room for one more touch, but not many.

case_0083.rationale: reason=payment_otp_timeout at step=payment_authentication with source=customer is a session that expired, not a refusal — importantly it is a timeout rather than an active cancel, which carries no signal of unwillingness at all. No authorisation exists for pay_1e3afee770d347, so a fresh link is the only mechanism that can work. Everything else says this recovers on the first attempt: tenure_days=1024, successful_payments=32, prior_failures_90d=0, prior_contacts_30d=0, and the 486.24 INR charge is almost exactly this AXIS customer's typical_invoice_paise of 47976 (479.76 INR), so there is no amount shock to explain the drop-off.

case_0109.rationale: reason=payment_failed from source=bank at payment_authorization gives no cause, as Razorpay notes is usual for YES_BANK-style issuer declines, so I decline to name one.
